source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity and 976,000 square feet of technical space, a ratio that implies a campus built for volume rather than the densest racks.

The two figures are the whole of what the operator states. No rack count, no design power density, and no tenant list appear, so any conversion from megawatts to accelerators is an outside estimate. At 40 kW per rack the 77 MW supports roughly 1,925 racks, and at 100 kW per rack roughly 770. The square footage is large against the power, which points to a floor plan that was not laid out around the highest-density equipment, though the spec page never says so directly.

The certifications describe what workloads the campus is eligible to host, not who hosts them. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes each cover a different compliance regime. None of them establishes that an AI tenant is present.

Within Texas, this campus ranks second by published megawatts among the 19 facilities that publish a figure, against a published state total of 475.41 MW. That is about a sixth of all publicly stated capacity in the state. Texas has 137 mapped facilities, and most publish no megawatt figure at all, so the 19-facility set is self-selected and small. The ranking shows this is one of the largest campuses in Texas that anyone has put a number on, not that it is the second largest in the state.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
